hints: Notice the question asks for the definition of potential difference across a component, where charge flows through and energy is converted.
Recall the governing relation $V = W/Q$ and that $1 \text{ V} = 1 \text{ J C}^{-1}$, so volts mean joules per coulomb.
Compare each option's divisor - charge, current, resistance, time - and ask which one gives joules per coulomb.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the meaning of potential difference $V$ for charge passing through an electrical component.
State the physical rule: when charge $Q$ moves through a potential difference $V$, energy $W$ is transferred, given by $W = QV$.
Rearrange to define potential difference: $V = W/Q$, so $V$ is energy transferred per unit charge.
Check units: energy in joules $\text{J}$ divided by charge in coulombs $\text{C}$ gives $\text{J C}^{-1}$, which is the volt $\text{V}$.
Energy per unit time is power, energy per unit current has no standard name, and energy per unit resistance is not a defined quantity.
Therefore the definition matches energy transferred per unit charge. This is option A

options.A: Potential difference is defined by $V = W/Q$, the energy $W$ transferred per unit charge $Q$ passing through the component.
options.B: Energy per unit current would be energy per charge per time, which does not give the volt and confuses charge with current.
options.C: Resistance is not the divisor in the definition of potential difference; $V = IR$ is a circuit relation, not the definition of $V$.
options.D: Energy transferred per unit time is power $P = W/t$, measured in watts, not potential difference measured in volts.
